base_override.reason: The engine's normalized base ($8.8309/share) is the FY2025 median print, anchored before the FY2026 mix step-up completed: gross margin 16.36% → 17.72% and operating income $1,827M → $2,109M (FY2025 → FY2026, fundamentals.json/financials_history.csv), corroborated by Q2 FY2026 (revenue +7.2% YoY, backlog +5.4%, funded +44%, guidance raised). FY2026 cash quality is clean (OCF $1,750M ≈ NI $1,448M + D&A $290M). The TTM pin ($16.2441/share, ttm.py) was rejected: TTM OCF of $2,300M is working-capital timing — TTM net income fell 1.85% YoY and FY2027 OCF is guided to ~$1.85B, below the TTM print. Measured impact: median base prints Tier C (weighted IRR 12.63%, IV@15% $99.56); this base prints Tier B (15.72%, $132.68); verdict sized to the conservative end with the method range stated.
base_override.source: This run's dcf_numbers.json base_oe_latest_per_share, built from financials_history.csv FY2026 row (period ended 2026-01-02): OCF $1,750,000,000 − capex $125,000,000 − SBC $95,000,000 = conservative OE $1,530,000,000 over 130,000,000 diluted shares = $11.7692/share. Declared under bounded authority (c): built exclusively from figures printed by this run's engine outputs; construction quoted in analysis.md (OVERRIDE).

moat_against: Monopsonist customer recompetes everything on price — Leidos has litigated Navy SMIT pricing; Booz Allen, CACI, SAIC, Parsons and the primes contest every award
Through-cycle ROIC ~10% (3.89% in FY2023) — the 17–19% of the last two years is unproven through a budget cycle
Gross margin 17.72% even after the mix shift — a services margin, not a product franchise margin
Federal budget/efficiency pressure hits the whole revenue base at once; growth leans on M&A (Entrust) and buybacks — Q2 organic revenue growth +3.9% vs +7.2% reported
moat_for: $48.71B backlog (~2.8x TTM revenue) with funded backlog +44% YoY to $10.22B — multi-year visibility
Incumbency on mission-critical classified programs (Navy SMIT, intelligence infrastructure); past-performance ratings and a cleared workforce are formal bid discriminators
Scale and breadth: $17.6B revenue across defense, intelligence, health and civil — can bid primes-sized integrations
Mix shift to defense-tech products: gross margin 13.98% (FY2023) → 17.72% (FY2026); ROIC proxy 16.94% / 19.10% in FY2025/26 (fundamentals.json)
moat_justification: Incumbency on classified mission programs, a cleared workforce and a $48.71B backlog (funded +44% YoY) are real advantages, and the defense-tech mix shift lifted gross margin from 13.98% (FY2023) to 17.72% (FY2026) with the ROIC proxy at 16.94%/19.10% in FY2025/26 — but through-cycle ROIC was ~10% (3.89% in the FY2023 impairment year), the US government is a monopsonist that recompetes all work on price, and the core product is cleared labor that Booz Allen, CACI, SAIC, Parsons and the primes also supply. Moderate/narrow moat, CAP 8.5 years.
name: Leidos Holdings, Inc.
one_liner: Quality government-services compounder at a mix inflection, moat 5/10 — clears 15% only on the latest audited FY base (weighted IRR 15.7%, IV@15% $132.68 vs $124.85) and only barely; on the standardized median base it is a C that clears 15% below ~$100, and the bear case ($90.73) sits well under the price — size it to the bear end.
